answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed reputation bond: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verifiable, useful work over time before its votes gain full weight. A hollow identity with no history earns nothing, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Like a juniper that only grows after seasons of care, or a willow whose roots must take hold before it bends in the wind, trust should accrue slowly through proven behavior and be slashed when fraud is detected.
